questions.title: Circular motion & simple harmonic motion — shadow projection

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The velocity and acceleration both have constant magnitude, and the velocity is always perpendicular to the acceleration (the velocity is tangential and the acceleration is directed towards the centre).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: v = Rω

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: a = Rω² = (Rω)ω = vω

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer: x = R sin θ

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: θ = ωt

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.answer: Substituting θ = ωt into x = R sin θ gives x = R sin ωt.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.answer: The equation is of the form x = x₀ sin ωt, the defining equation of simple harmonic motion (with amplitude x₀ = R), so the shadow's motion is simple harmonic.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.answer: amplitude = diameter/2 = 0.46/2 = 0.23 m

parts.label: (e)
parts.answer: The shadow is at the extreme of its motion — at the left-hand edge of the circular path (maximum displacement from P), labelled A, where the acceleration is a maximum.

questions.title: The first law of thermodynamics — pumping, boiling & vaporisation

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The internal energy can be changed by (1) work done on or by the system, and (2) thermal energy supplied to or removed from the system.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: Pumping quickly gives no time for thermal energy to be transferred to or from the gas, while work is done on the gas to compress it (decrease its volume). From the first law ΔU = q + W (with q = 0), the internal energy increases, so the temperature rises.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: During vaporisation the molecular separation increases, so the heating increases the potential energy of the molecules while their kinetic energy is unchanged. Since temperature depends on the kinetic energy, the temperature stays at 100 °C.

questions.title: Gravitational field — point masses & two spheres

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The force per unit mass acting on a small test mass placed at the point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: F = GMm/x² and g = F/m, so g = [GMm/x²]/m = GM/x², where G is the gravitational constant.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer: An arrow at P pointing directly towards the point mass.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: The field at Q is in the opposite direction to that at P (towards the mass), and is four times the field strength at P (Q is at distance x/2, and g ∝ 1/x²).

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: A line starting at (R, −g₀) and ending at (L − R, +g₀), passing through (L/2, 0), becoming shallower from R to L/2 and steeper again from L/2 to L − R.

questions.title: Absolute zero & ideal gas — molecules, moles & r.m.s. speed

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.answer: temperature = −273.15 °C

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.answer: temperature = 0 K

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer: The graph is a straight line through the origin (pV ∝ kT), so the gas is ideal.

questions.title: Electric potential — the hydrogen atom dipole

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The work done per unit positive charge in moving a small test charge from infinity to the point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
V = (e/4πε₀)(1/10 pm − 1/110 pm) — the proton contributes +e/4πε₀r and the electron −e/4πε₀r.
V = (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹/4π × 8.85 × 10⁻¹²) × [(10⁻¹ − 110⁻¹) × 10¹²] = 130 V

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: A cross at the midpoint between the electron and the proton (x = 60 pm), where the +e and −e potentials cancel.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer: A curve from (10, +130) to (110, −130), getting shallower until x = 60 pm, crossing V = 0 at (60, 0), then getting steeper, and passing through (30, +32) and (90, −32).

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer:
Series: QS = Q₁ = Q₂ and VS = V₁ + V₂.
Parallel: QS = Q₁ + Q₂ and VS = V₁ = V₂.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
The total charge is unchanged and the total capacitance is (470 + 180) × 10⁻⁶ F.
E = Q²/2C = (4.23 × 10⁻³)²/(2 × 650 × 10⁻⁶)
= 14 mJ

questions.title: Faraday’s law — induced e.m.f. across an aircraft’s wings

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The induced e.m.f. is (directly) proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux (linkage).

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.answer:
e.m.f. = ΔΦ/Δt, so flux = e.m.f. × time = 0.54 × 15
= 8.1 Wb

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer:
area = speed × time × width, so v = area/(time × width) = 2.1 × 10⁵/(15 × 68)
= 210 m s⁻¹

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.answer: By Lenz’s law the induced current produces an opposing force which must act backwards. From Fleming’s left-hand rule the current in the wings is therefore from Q to P. Inside an e.m.f. source the current flows from − to +, so P is at the higher potential.

questions.title: Uranium-238 alpha decay — mass, gamma wavelength & neutrinos

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: A packet/quantum of energy of electromagnetic radiation.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.answer:
The gamma photon carries the remaining energy: 4.274 − 4.200 = 0.074 MeV.
E = hc/λ, so λ = hc/E = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 3.00 × 10⁸)/(0.074 × 1.60 × 10⁻¹³)
= 1.7 × 10⁻¹¹ m

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.answer: The true energy of the gamma photon is smaller (the thorium nucleus carries some kinetic energy), so the true wavelength is larger than the calculated value.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Beta decay also emits (anti)neutrinos, and the particles emitted in beta decay carry varying amounts of energy, so the energy of the gamma photon is variable between decays — there is no single wavelength.

questions.title: Wien’s law & luminosity — conclusions about star X

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The temperature is inversely proportional to the wavelength at which the maximum emission occurs (λmax ∝ 1/T), where T is the thermodynamic temperature of the star’s surface.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: Any three of: star X has a surface temperature of 7000 K (higher than the Sun’s 5770 K); star X has a higher luminosity than the Sun; the luminosity of star X is 2.7 × 10²⁷ W; the radius of star X is 1.3 × 10⁹ m.

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The light from star X is red-shifted (the galaxy is receding from the Earth), so the wavelength of the peak emission would be greater than its true value.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The product of the density of the medium and the speed of sound in the medium (Z = ρc).

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: The ultrasound waves cause the crystal to vibrate, and these vibrations generate an induced e.m.f. across the crystal, which is then detected.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.answer:
Intensity reflection coefficient = (Z₁ − Z₂)²/(Z₁ + Z₂)²
= (40.4 − 1.48)²/(40.4 + 1.48)² = 0.86

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.answer: The Z values of body tissue and water are very similar, so almost all the ultrasound is transmitted (almost none is reflected).
